title: The Country In Which, The Group With Which

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know relative clauses with *el que* and a preposition from B1 Unit 20: the preposition goes before *el que*, *la que*, *los que* or *las que*, and the article matches the noun (*el edificio en el que vivimos*). They are the tool for describing movements: the country in which protests began, the group with which a song is linked.

items.spanish: Chile es el país en el que empezaron las protestas de 2019.
items.english: Chile is the country in which the 2019 protests began.

items.spanish: Ni Una Menos es el movimiento en el que participan muchas jóvenes.
items.english: Ni Una Menos is the movement in which many young women take part.

items.spanish: Las Tesis es el colectivo con el que se asocia la canción Un violador en tu camino.
items.english: Las Tesis is the group with which the song Un violador en tu camino is associated.

items.spanish: El pañuelo verde es el símbolo con el que se identifican muchas manifestantes.
items.english: The green scarf is the symbol with which many protesters identify.

sections.content: Keep the preposition that the verb needs (*participar en*, *asociar con*) and match the article to the noun: *el movimiento en el que*, *la marcha en la que*. Without the preposition the sentence is wrong: not *el país que empezaron las protestas*.
